title: Realms
intro: Host-created RuntimeRealm instances own separate global objects, intrinsic graphs, descriptors and module state. One agent can own multiple realms. Coverage is bounded by the implemented intrinsic and host entry points rather than a complete general host realm-control API.

entries.notes: RuntimeLifecycle creates or joins an explicit agent-cluster/agent/realm ownership graph. Agents may own multiple realms; entered execution frames select and restore the current realm, including exception unwinding and asynchronous continuation paths. A complete general JavaScript host realm-control API is not implied.

Every realm owns its intrinsic prototypes, built-in function identities and descriptor baseline. Lazy initialization preserves identity within a realm and isolates mutations across realms, including supported cross-realm constructor prototype fallback. This describes the implemented intrinsic surface, not support for every ECMA-262 built-in.

GlobalThis bootstraps supported default bindings against the owning realm's intrinsic graph. Realms keep distinct globals, descriptors, module bindings and namespace caches; subsequent user mutations are not overwritten by repeated bootstrap.
